title: artifacts/run_manifest.json
description: The record of what actually ran. Principle V requires every reported number to trace to a computation that executed; this file is the root of that trace. Written by store/manifest.py.

run_id.description: Content-derived, not time-derived: sha256 of (config digest + root seed + code revision), truncated. A time-derived id would change between two runs that are supposed to be byte-identical, which would defeat the determinism test that this manifest is meant to support.

seed_override.description: Set when --seed was passed, so a run that did not use the configured seed cannot be mistaken for one that did.

digest.description: sha256 over all config files, sorted by path.

resolved.description: The fully merged config as actually used, embedded verbatim. Recorded because reading the config files later shows what they say now, not what they said during the run.

code_revision.description: git rev-parse HEAD, or null outside a repository. Null is recorded rather than omitted so an unversioned run is visibly unversioned.

code_dirty.description: True when the working tree had uncommitted changes. A metric produced from a dirty tree is not reproducible from the recorded revision, and the manifest must say so.

packages.description: Installed version per direct dependency. numpy and shap are recorded together deliberately: the SHAP numba kernels are ABI-bound to the numpy version, so this pair explains a class of failure that no other field would.

data_inputs.description: The raw source files consumed, with size and digest. Provenance is documented in docs/data-provenance.md; this is the per-run evidence that the documented files are the ones that were read.

status.description: 'reused_cached' and 'succeeded' are distinguished so a report cannot claim a number was recomputed when it was read from a previous run's artifact. 'skipped_upstream' distinguishes a stage that was switched off from one whose dependency was.

sha256.description: For CSV and JSON, the digest of the file. For Parquet, the digest of a canonical sorted projection rather than the file, because Parquet writers embed library metadata that varies between environments. research.md section 12 records why byte-identity is claimed for the submission only.

gates.description: The pass/fail record for each enforced guarantee. Present in the manifest so the guarantees are visible in the same artifact as the results they qualify, rather than in a separate file a reader might not open.

forward_leak_columns.description: Feature names that failed either the outcome-name screen or the forward-perturbation check. Non-empty means exit code 3.

model_id.description: Read from config, never a literal in code. Recorded per run because hosted model availability changes and a metric attributed to the wrong model is a Principle V failure.
